bio: I am a junior in Mechanical Engineering with a minor in Robotics at Carnegie Mellon University. I expect to graduate in May 2028. I transferred from Penn State, where I studied Aerospace Engineering.
I work on embedded hardware, aero structures, manufacturing, and AI-driven CAD. Most of my projects mix mechanical design with electronics and firmware.
I am looking for a Summer 2027 internship in product design and engineering, propulsion, manufacturing, space, or automotive. I am open to any location.

timeline.org: Visual Design Engineering Lab (VDEL), Carnegie Mellon University
timeline.role: Undergraduate Researcher, Generative Manufacturing Design (Prof. Levent Burak Kara)
bullets: Building an LLM pipeline that converts natural language and reference images into parametric CAD through SysML part models. Industry-sponsored; pending journal publication.
Part sizes are grounded in published literature and current supply-chain data. Compiler repair and vision scoring automatically fix invalid designs.
Validating DFM rules on the KERF project by scoring AI-generated CAD against machined walls, holes, and corners.
Designed and machined the body tube for the rocket airframe. FEA showed a safety factor of 2 under 20 g launch loads.
Earned NAR/TRA Level 1 high-power rocketry certification. Built and flew an L1 rocket to 1,100 ft apogee; recovered intact.
Working on an L2 rocket with a custom STM32 flight computer and machined avionics bay (in progress).
Designed vortex generators in SolidWorks and simulated them in Ansys Fluent: about 10 N downforce change at 50 mph for a 10% drag penalty. Concluded they were not worth adding.

timeline.role: B.S. Mechanical Engineering, Minor in Robotics
bullets: Relevant coursework: Circuits, Statics, Strength of Materials, Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics.
In progress: Mechanical Design, Heat Transfer, Dynamics.
Simulated cabin ventilation flow in Ansys Fluent across 5 operating conditions to characterize duct pressure drop. Delivered the findings to the team in a formal report.
Ran First Article Inspection on 3 parts against engineering drawings and cleared them for production release.
Modeled as-built vs. nominal geometry in SolidWorks to document supplier and in-house non-conformances.
Wrote and revised test plans and interior component drawings for class dividers and bulkheads.

timeline.org: Applied Research Laboratory, Penn State University
bullets: Screened 2 functional metal-oxide compositions for phase stability using Thermo-Calc CALPHAD databases.
Implemented a revised structure-search algorithm in MATLAB and C++. It cut convergence time by 20% compared to the group's prior method.

projects.title: Natural-Language-to-CAD Pipeline
projects.summary: LLM pipeline that turns natural-language requests and reference images into parametric CAD.
projects.team: Team (VDEL, CMU, Prof. Levent Burak Kara)
projects.goal: Turn a natural-language request and a reference image into a parametric CAD part, in a way where each failure can be traced back to either the design intent or the generated code.
did: Requests map to SysML part stereotypes, then to a JSON design representation, then to KCL code. Each step can be checked on its own.
Compiler errors feed an automated repair loop.
A vision check renders the part and scores it against the reference image.
Part sizes are grounded in published literature and current supply-chain data.
Validating DFM rules on the KERF project by scoring AI-generated CAD against machined walls, holes, and corners.
results: Industry-sponsored. Pending journal publication (no link yet).
TODO: quantitative results once they can be shared.

projects.title: L2 Certification Rocket (Tripoli)
projects.summary: Fiberglass high-power rocket with a dual-deploy avionics bay, flown to 3,000 ft for TRA Level 2.
projects.coverAlt: Rocket on the launch rail next to labeled CAD of the avionics bay
projects.goal: Design, build, and fly a fiberglass high-power rocket for Tripoli Rocketry Association (TRA) Level 2 certification, with an avionics bay that deploys the parachutes.
did: Designed the rocket and the avionics bay in SolidWorks.
Cut the fiberglass tubes with a wet tile saw; cut the fiberglass fins and bulkheads on a waterjet.
Ran flight simulations in OpenRocket to check the design.
Applied epoxy to the fins and bulkheads for strength.
Built the avionics bay: a 3D-printed sled between fiberglass bulkheads, holding two flight computers, a 9V battery, a LiPo battery, and a screw-switch mount.
